transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-06-02 Time: 15:00 UTC Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lucas Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Ruiz (Sunridge CISO), Michael Cho (Head of Eng), Sara Benson (Compliance), Evan Park (Cloud Architect)

Summary: Quick posture review focusing on SOC 2 / ISO 27001 artifacts, access to trust center, RBAC/SSO, audit log retention and encryption/KMS, plus data residency. Conversation had some audio drop at 00:12 but otherwise clear.

[00:00] Lucas: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lucas from Redwood. Priya and I will run through our SOC 2 / ISO posture and answer any compliance questions you have.
[00:12] Dana: Thanks, Lucas. We've got a fairly tight vendor assessment window; need to confirm SOC 2 Type II and ISO mappings. Also curious about Trust Center access.
[00:25] Priya: Yeah, totally. We can give read-only access to our Trust Center where you can download the SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scope. The usual is we provide the report and a controls mapping spreadsheet.
[00:38] Michael: For our procurement team, can you confirm if the SOC 2 is full Type II and what the coverage dates are?
[00:45] Lucas: It's SOC 2 Type II covering Jan-Dec 2025, cover services: hosted API, dedicated instances, private deployments. Note sometimes the auto-transcript uses slightly different product names but the report itself lists services.
[00:59] Sara: On ISO 27001, we need a controls mapping showing how your policies map to Annex A controls.
[01:08] Priya: We've got that. We'll share a controls mapping spreadsheet. It includes control, Redwood control owner, evidence location in the Trust Center, and typical artifacts like policy docs, AIP/DR runbooks.
[01:25] Evan: About Trust Center access: is that self-serve? Or do you provision per-company? We prefer a per-company role with SSO.
[01:35] Lucas: We provision per-customer read-only access and tie it to SSO via SAML/SCIM. We can integrate with Azure AD, Okta. You can also request access to specific artifacts only.
[01:47] Dana: Great. On SSO and RBAC, our security team requires role separation and admin logging. How granular is Redwood's RBAC?
[01:55] Priya: We have role-based roles —org admin, billing, viewer, and a bunch of finer-grain roles for console actions and API keys. We log admin actions and can export audit trails. The console supports SCIM provisioning to sync groups.
[02:10] Michael: Is that available for Private deployments as well, or is it only for hosted?
[02:17] Priya: For Private (VPC/on-prem) the control plane is customer-isolated; you can run our SSO integration on your side. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM or kept in our tenant, depending on the deployment model.
[02:33] Dana: Shipping logs to our SIEM is preferred — we need 12 months retention and tamper-evident logs.
[02:40] Lucas: We support log export to S3, GCS, and direct syslog/Splunk endpoints. Retention is configurable; default is 90 days but can be extended. For tamper evidence we support signed log delivery and integration with immutable storage buckets.
[02:58] Evan: On encryption — at rest and in transit — what KMS options? Do you support customer-managed keys (CMKs)?
[03:06] Priya: Yes. For hosted we offer platform-managed keys by default, and customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault for dedicated/private. We have envelope encryption and the option to rotate keys per-customer.
[03:20] Michael: If we bring our own KMS for Private, are there any functional tradeoffs?
[03:27] Priya: Functionality is the same; some telemetry and deep observability features require additional configuration to avoid exfiltration of keys. In Private you control the KMS and we operate within those constraints.
[03:40] Dana: Data residency — our policy requires all PHI to stay in the US East region. How do you guarantee that?
[03:49] Lucas: We have region pinning and routing policies. For hosted customers you can choose region constraints; for Dedicated you get a dedicated pool in a selected region. For Private, obviously you control the network and physical location.
[04:05] Sara: About evidence — procurement asked for sample audit logs and access logs. Are those downloadable?
[04:12] Priya: We can provide redacted samples. Full raw logs are sensitive, so we usually provide exports with PII masked. If you need full logs under NDA that's doable for on-prem or dedicated environments.
[04:25] Lucas: Quick note: sometimes the transcript generator mashes 'KV cache' into different words, so in the controls mapping we'll be explicit about technical terms.
[04:34] Dana: Any pen test reports or third-party attestations?
[04:38] Lucas: Yes—we have a recent pen test summary and an external vulnerability scan report. The full pen test report is shared under NDA; the summary is in Trust Center.
[04:50] Evan: For ISO specific controls, can you show how change management and configuration management map?
[04:56] Priya: Absolutely. Our controls mapping ties change requests to Jira tickets, code review evidence, deployment runbooks, and the CMDB snapshot for configuration items. We'll include those references.
[05:12] Michael: For our legal team, any standard data processing addendum and breach notification SLA?
[05:18] Lucas: Standard DPA is available. Breach notification SLA: we'll notify within 72 hours, with more details in the DPA and incident response playbook.
[05:29] Sara: Curious about retention policies — tokens, logs, and model inputs. How long do you keep user prompts and embeddings?
[05:38] Priya: By default we don't persist customer prompts for hosted inference beyond short-term caching used for caching and rate limiting; customers can opt in/out. For Dedicated and Private, retention is controlled by customer policies. We'll include exact retention settings in the Trust Center docs.
[05:55] Dana: We also have a question about model artifacts — are they shared across tenants or isolated?
[06:01] Priya: Models are isolated by tenant. We use shared base images but per-tenant model weights and KV caches are segregated. For Dedicated/Private customers you get isolated model instances.
[06:15] Lucas: Any other big blockers?
[06:18] Michael: Cost is not the blocker; it's more about evidence and timeline for compliance teams.
[06:23] Dana: Right. If we can get SOC 2 Type II, controls mapping, and Trust Center access this week, procurement can move quickly.
[06:30] Priya: We'll prioritize. I'll assemble the controls mapping and sample artifacts.
[06:35] Lucas: I'll share the Trust Center link and the SOC 2 PDF after the call.
[06:40] Evan: Can we get a quick demo of audit log export and KMS integration in the follow-up?
[06:46] Priya: Yes, we'll do a technical deep dive and demo. We'll run a sample log export to S3 and show CMK rotation.
[06:55] Sara: On the ISO mapping, our auditors prefer a table that maps each Annex A control to evidence. That's what we'll need.
[07:03] Priya: Understood — that's exactly what we provide.
[07:07] Lucas: Ok let's do a quick recap of next steps.
[07:10] Lucas: Action items — Redwood: Trust Center + SOC 2 PDF (Lucas), ISO controls mapping and artifacts (Priya). Sunridge: reviewer list and data residency specifics (Evan/Dana). We'll schedule demo for audit log export and KMS by mid-June.
[07:28] Dana: Sounds good, thanks.
[07:31] Lucas: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links.

End of transcript.
